hartsy_current: partial: Vulkan and CUDA, unused. VulkanBackend quantizes Q and K with the four transforms (H4, H64, signed and padded H128) and attends with u8 probabilities and F32 state (QuantizeInt8AttentionRows, QuantizeInt8AttentionKeys, QuantizeInt8AttentionValues, QuantizeInt8AttentionQueries; Int8AttentionU8): unmasked, per-key K scales, keys centered by their mean over one segment, F32 operands at padded head dim 64, 128 or 256. No representative-key center, no thread-class K scales, no masks. On CUDA the INT8 attention v2 rows (F32 or F16 operands, head dim 128) rotate Q and the mean-centered K before quantizing them when numerics.int8AttnV2Rotate is set; it is off by default and nothing sets it. The transform follows the pinned rule: H4 up to 256 keys, signed H128 past that; H64 and padded H128 are refused at head dim 128, as the reference refuses them. One added launch (int8_attn_v2_rot) writes the Q and K bytes and scales; V, its scales and the attention launch are the shipped ones, and V is not rotated. With the knob set and that kernel not loaded the rows decline, so a call asked to rotate never runs unrotated. A captured graph replays the launches chosen when it was captured, whatever the knob says later. The same limits hold as on Vulkan: no representative-key center, no thread-class K scales, no masks
disposition: Out of PR 01 production implementation; required later port, cannot be excluded at completion.
status_evidence: RTX 3060 and RTX 4090, both at commit 5472c0393: every quantized operand and the attention output bit-equal to Int8AttentionV2Reference run with Int8AttentionExp2.Evaluate as its exp2 (Int8AttentionQuantizeVulkanTests, Int8AttentionCenteringVulkanTests, Int8AttentionQueriesVulkanTests, Int8AttentionU8VulkanTests), except output values below 2^-100 where the reference carries a subnormal float and both cards read it as zero. The RTX 4090 run also had one unrelated test that fails on that host on main (Kimi.PackedMoeTests). The reference's transforms and selection rule are pinned to the Kitchen kernel's constants in Int8AttentionRotationTests; there is no Kitchen-generated vector for the INT8 output, so this is not a runtime parity claim against the Kitchen kernel. A descriptive timing on the RTX 3060 for 1,024 by 1,024 unmasked attention: about 10 times faster than the exact F32 route and 10 to 14 times slower than the F16 cooperative-matrix route, with about 12 times that route's error. No caller, no planner row. CUDA (Int8AttentionRotationCudaTests): on the RTX 3060 at commit 084ce81a9, 44 cases (unrotated through the new kernel, H4, signed H128 and the pinned selection; F32 and F16 operands; the refusals and the kernel-not-loaded case) at 64 to 1,100 keys, among them 1,024 by 1,024 through the public route with a grouped call. In every case that quantizes: every Q, K and V byte, every scale and every key mean equal to Int8AttentionV2Reference.Quantize, and the u8-probability output bit-equal to Int8AttentionV2Reference replayed on the kernel's own exp2; the F16-probability row's output within 1e-5 relative L2 of the reference on its own exp2. On the RTX 4090 at commit 07ac629e8, the 37 cases that existed then, at 64 to 333 keys, passed, and the rotation kernel rebuilt there is byte-identical to the committed PTX; the 1,024-token cases ran on the RTX 3060 only. No timing on a quiet machine: every RTX 3060 sample of Int8AttentionRotationCudaTimingTests was taken under CPU load. No caller: the planner reaches these rows only when numerics.int8AttnV2 and the rotation knob are both set. Equality is with the emulator, not the Kitchen kernel.

hartsy_current: partial: Vulkan only, unused. The quantize entries and Int8AttentionU8 are separate calls, so quantized Q, K and V can be kept and attended again; nothing keeps or reuses them. CUDA quantizes inside each call, into a workspace its attention launch reads at once: with numerics.int8AttnV2Rotate set (default off, nothing sets it) the Q and K it writes are the reference's rotated operands for H4 and signed H128 at head dim 128, but no entry hands them to a caller or attends operands quantized earlier

status_evidence: RTX 3060 and RTX 4090, both at commit 5472c0393: the operands the Vulkan quantize entries write are bit-equal to Int8AttentionV2Reference.Quantize, and Int8AttentionU8 over them gives the reference's output, as recorded under sage-rotation. On CUDA the operands the INT8 v2 rows write with the knob set equal Int8AttentionV2Reference.Quantize on the cards and at the sizes recorded under sage-rotation; they are read back through a test hook only. Reuse itself has no test, and no reuse count is timed. Not a runtime parity claim against the Kitchen kernel.
